subject: StackWise replacement economics and bundling clarification
messages:
From: Evan Clarke <evan@stackwise.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stackwise.com, Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@stackwise.com>
Date: 2026-03-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: Exploring replacement: cost & bundle questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking the quick call earlier. We're evaluating replacing our current inference provider (Fogline) and want to understand unit economics and how you would price a replacement with comparable features. A few quick facts about our usage: attached is an anonymized export (stackwise-usage-export.csv) with monthly token volumes, peak concurrency windows, and embedding counts.

Top asks for this stage:
- A clear line-item comparison to Fogline's quote (they offered a blended token rate + an embeddings add-on).
- Packaging options for predictable spend (commit tiers vs. pay-as-you-go).
- Any migration credits or onboarding assistance you can offer.

For context, Fogline's commercial sheet is attached (fogline-quote.pdf). They are pushing a 12-month term with a 20% discount on list + two months of free pilot credits. Can Redwood match on blended economics and provide an equivalent or better migration path?

Appreciate a concise comparison — our procurement team would like to close this assessment this month.

Best,
Evan
Evan Clarke
Head of Platform Procurement
StackWise

Attachments: fogline-quote.pdf, stackwise-usage-export.csv

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Evan Clarke <evan@stackwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-26T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement: cost & bundle questions

Hi Evan — thanks for the data and the note. I reviewed the Fogline sheet and your usage export. High level: we can get materially closer on blended unit economics while offering better predictability and lower latency for your embed-heavy workloads.

Key differences I'll highlight in a short write-up (attaching initial offer):
- Pricing: two model — commit-based credits (monthly commit) vs consumption. For your profile the commit model reduces effective token cost by ~18% at your 12mo forecast.
- Embeddings: bundled as a separate SKU but we can roll up into a blended commitment for billing simplicity.
- Migration: we typically offer a migration credit structure (one-time onboarding credit + first-month usage credit) and a dedicated technical onboarding block.

Next steps: I attached redwood-stackwise-offer-v1.pdf with a compact comparison matrix and a preliminary credit proposal. Can you confirm the following so we can firm numbers?
1) Which Fogline line items are non-negotiable (e.g., pilot credits or SLA terms)?
2) Do you need the embedding workload carved out separately for contractual reasons?

If you prefer, Marissa (cc'd) can run a short econ table and I can follow with a proposed legal term sheet.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-stackwise-offer-v1.pdf

From: Evan Clarke <evan@stackwise.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stackwise.com, Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@stackwise.com>
Date: 2026-03-30T10:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement: cost & bundle questions

Jonas — thanks. Quick answers inline:
1) Fogline non-negotiables: the two-month pilot credit (they're offering $75k of pilot credit in total) and a 99.9% SLA with financial crediting for downtime.
2) Embeddings are considered a separate contract line by our BI team, but we'd prefer a blended invoice if possible.

Procurement asked for a firm written match (or better) on the formatted commercial sheet — they want an apples-to-apples run rate we can take to the CFO. Can you (a) produce a line-by-line comparison, and (b) confirm the maximum migration credit you can put into an LOI?

Thanks,
Evan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: FW: Exploring replacement: cost & bundle questions

Jonas / Karthik — looping you in with a quick econ view. I ran the usage file against our pricing models. Summary:
- If we do a 12-month commit at 80% of their forecasted volume, effective token rate is about 16% lower than Fogline's post-discount list.
- Embedding costs if bundled into the commit reduce overall blended by another ~3-4%.
- Migration credit: recommendation is $60k one-time onboarding + $40k first-month usage credit (total $100k) and 3 days of dedicated eng time for migration.

Concerns: Margin impact on the first-year P&L if we give full parity + $100k credit. Suggested push: exchange the $100k credit for a signed 12mo commit at 90% of forecast and (optionally) an extended 30-day pilot escrow instead of free credits.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with scenarios (internal only). If that trade is acceptable we can draft a LOI and send a redline-friendly commercial sheet.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-internal-econ-scenarios.xlsx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Evan Clarke <evan@stackwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@stackwise.com>, procurement@stackwise.com
Date: 2026-04-04T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Exploring replacement: cost & bundle questions

Hi Evan / Lara / procurement team —

Appreciate the patience while we worked the numbers internally. Attached is redwood-stackwise-offer-v2.pdf and a short migration SLA summary (migration-sla-summary.pdf). High level of the offer: 

- Commercial: We will match Fogline's effective blended run rate for year 1 on the volumes you provided, conditional on a 12-month committed spend at 90% of the provided forecast. This includes embedding usage rolled into the blended rate (single invoice).
- Credits: Instead of the two-month pilot credit, we will provide:
  * $60,000 onboarding credit (applied to initial professional services invoice)
  * $40,000 first-month usage credit (applied as invoice credit)
  Total migration credit: $100,000.
- SLA: 99.9% regional SLA on inference with financial crediting; migration-SLA summary attached with rollback playbook.
- Operational: Dedicated onboarding engineer for 3 days and prioritized queue for first 30 days post-cutover.

If that structure meets your procurement bar I can get legal to draft an LOI/Order Form with the commercial table line-for-line versus Fogline's sheet (we'll include the comparison table in the exhibit).

If you need any adjustments to term length, we can consider a 24-month option for additional 6% discount on blended unit economics.

Thanks — ready to move to LOI once you confirm.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-stackwise-offer-v2.pdf, migration-sla-summary.pdf
